statement: Let tau_0 be empty, and for every integer n>=0 obtain tau_(n+1) by taking the disjoint union of tau_n with a singleton and then adjoining a new minimum. Let Q_n consist of the nonnegative real vectors on the 2n vertices satisfying sum_(v in I) x_v <= |I| for every lower ideal I of tau_n, and let h_n(t)=sum_(a in Q_n intersect Z^(2n)) t^(number of positive coordinates of a), with h_0(t)=1. For an indeterminate t, define F(t,x)=sum_(n>=0) t^(-n) h_n(t) x^(n+1) and R(t,x)=sum_(m>=1) (-1)^(m-1) [1+(1+t)^m t^(1-m) sum_(j=0)^(m-2) t^j] x^m, where the inner sum is zero for m=1. Then R(t,F(t,x))=x=F(t,R(t,x)) in Q(t)[[x]]. Equivalently, the same R is x/[(1+x)(1+(1+t)x)(1+(1+t)x/t)] and is the compositional inverse of the full support-refined comb generating series. This is the entire identity frozen in source.md, with no restriction to a finite range or scalar specialization of t.
contribution: A complete proof proposed for fresh review of the final unnumbered comb inverse proposal in Chapoton and Athanasiadis, arXiv:2605.26916v1, Section 9.6. The proof reduces every lower-ideal inequality to prefix costs, preserves the support statistic through local pair weights, and proves a bijection with ordered forests having a canonical first leaf, including the exact z(1+t) normalization. Formal elimination then yields the asserted inverse at all degrees. Weighted-tree inversion is classical, and the recent general support-duality theorem of Wang et al. is acknowledged as prior work but is not a dependency. No equivalent comb inverse resolution was found in the primary passages inspected on 2026-09-14 Asia/Shanghai; global priority is not certified. Fresh mathematical acceptance is pending.
